name: Phenethyl isothiocyanate (PEITC)
short: Oral cancer trial, 72 patients: no serious intervention-related adverse events with PEITC-fortified food. Smoker trials: no adverse-event data. Watercress (a PEITC source) altered 2 drugs' metabolism.
text: In a 2023 blinded, randomized, placebo-controlled trial, 72 patients with advanced oral or oropharyngeal cancer ate a texture-modified food fortified with PEITC, or the same food without it, for 12 weeks; adverse events were a measured outcome, and no serious intervention-related adverse events occurred in either group. The abstract does not report mild or moderate adverse events. Two randomized crossover trials gave PEITC by mouth for a week to cigarette smokers (82 completed one trial; 79 were randomized in the other) to study how it changes the metabolism of tobacco carcinogens; their abstracts give no adverse-event data. Interactions: a 2014 review states that PEITC changes the activity and expression of many drug-metabolising enzymes. In studies of watercress, a vegetable that contains PEITC as a conjugate (not PEITC itself), a single serving of watercress homogenate raised blood levels (AUC) of chlorzoxazone, a probe drug for the enzyme CYP2E1, by 56% in 10 healthy volunteers, and in 7 volunteers it lowered the oxidative breakdown products of acetaminophen (paracetamol); in 15 healthy non-smokers, however, eating watercress, which that abstract calls an excellent source of PEITC, did not change total excretion of 7-hydroxycoumarin, the product of coumarin breakdown by the enzyme CYP2A6, although more of it was excreted 2 to 4 hours after coumarin was given than before watercress, which the authors say suggests a delay in coumarin breakdown; they conclude that, under their study conditions, watercress had at most a marginal inhibitory effect on this reaction. No case reports of harm from PEITC were found in the cited sources.
